R663.note: Drops the second decode, rejects multi-component filenames, and canonicalizes with toRealPath()+startsWith() against the real base dir - closes both the double-decode bypass and symlink escape cleanly.

R664.note: Extension allowlist plus UUID-based safe filename closes CWE-434 as intended; response still reports the real destination path so nothing is silently hidden from the caller.

R665.note: Removes the /e eval but still invokes $formatter($value) where both the function name and argument remain fully attacker-controlled (via $_POST), so system/exec/passthru RCE is still directly reachable - the vector is not actually closed, just relocated.

R666.note: Extension whitelist + magic-byte MIME sniff + random filename correctly closes the upload vector, but the handler still returns only WriteHeader(201) with no body - the generated safe filename is never disclosed to the caller, so a legitimate uploader has no way to retrieve their own avatar afterward, and this is not mentioned.

R667.note: Swapping BinaryFormatter for JsonDocument is the accepted remediation for this un-fixable sink, but it silently breaks the wire format: any existing BinaryFormatter-serialized payload now always 400s, and cache consumers expecting the prior deserialized object type now get a JsonElement - the write-up claims this 'preserves the intended functionality,' which is not accurate.

R668.note: Write path is fixed correctly (content-validated, UUID filename), but the paired avatar_lookup.go (ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename)) is left completely untouched despite the contract explicitly requiring the read path be updated in step; the write-up asserts it 'remains safe' without justifying how a caller keyed on the original filename still finds the file.

R669.note: fgets() closes the stack overflow, but the fix never detects the case where fgets fills the 64-byte line buffer without hitting a newline - it silently accepts and returns 0 with a truncated line instead of rejecting per the contract, and never drains the unread remainder of stdin, corrupting the next call exactly as the contract warns against.

R670.note: Minimal, correct removal of @csrf_exempt (and its now-unused import); response shapes for 405/401/200 are untouched, matching the stated contract exactly.

R671.note: ArgumentList plus a strict alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist fully closes both metacharacter injection and the batch-file cmd.exe reentry risk, but the allowlist is a new restriction not called for by any stated contract and could reject legitimate report names the original accepted (e.g. containing spaces).

R672.note: Narrow request DTO decoded from gob, privileged fields (IsAdmin, Balance) set server-side - textbook mass-assignment fix with no other observable change.

R673.note: Swaps plain wtforms.Form for FlaskForm + validate_on_submit(), which performs its own CSRF check independent of app-wide CSRFProtect; no other behavior change to the file in scope.

R674.note: Captures clientId into a local before the call that may free req; same log message and return codes, no other observable change - clean minimal UAF fix.

R675.note: Adds secure=True as the CWE-614 finding requires; no other behavior changed.

R676.note: The character allowlist regex omits the double-quote character, so no string literal can ever be passed to lookupRate() - this breaks all legitimate lookupRate("key") calls the contract requires to keep working, while never implementing the approved-key allowlist on configKey that the contract actually asks for; write-up incorrectly claims lookupRate("discount_tier") still works.

R677.note: Removes trust in client-supplied mimetype, validates actual content via file-type magic-byte detection post-write, derives extension from detected type, cleans up on rejection - correct shape for this sink with no unstated behavior change.
